headline: Inclusion is active welcome—making space for people to belong and contribute as they are
universal_truth: Diversity is presence; inclusion is participation; you can be present without belonging
fun_facts: Employees who feel included are 3x more likely to be engaged at work
Inclusion isn't passive tolerance—it requires active effort to welcome and integrate
The opposite of exclusion isn't just presence—it's genuine belonging
discussion_questions: When have you felt included versus just tolerated?
How do you actively include others?
What barriers to inclusion exist in your environments?

hook.script: You can be in a room without being part of the conversation. You can be on a team without being welcomed. Inclusion isn't just presence—it's belonging. Making room means actively creating space where everyone can contribute.

cliff.script: Diversity gets people in the room. But what makes them actually feel welcome? What's the difference between presence and inclusion?

options.text: Inclusion requires active welcome—not just allowing presence but creating belonging; it means inviting contribution, valuing difference, and removing barriers to participation
options.response: Yes. Inclusion is a verb—it takes action. Diverse people can be present and still excluded through culture, assumption, and inaction. Active inclusion creates actual belonging.

options.text: Inclusion means treating everyone the same
options.response: Treating people the same can actually exclude—different people need different things to belong...

fact1.title: Passive vs Active
fact1.script: Passive inclusion says 'you're allowed to be here.' Active inclusion says 'we want you here and value what you bring.' The difference determines whether presence becomes belonging.

fact2.title: Barrier Removal
fact2.script: Inclusion requires removing barriers—not just opening doors but clearing paths. What prevents participation? What makes contribution difficult? Identifying and removing barriers creates inclusion.

fact3.title: Your Role
fact3.script: You can create inclusion wherever you are. Welcome the newcomer. Invite the quiet person to speak. Notice who's missing from conversations. Inclusion is practiced by individuals, not just organizations.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Diversity is presence; inclusion is participation. You can be present without belonging. Actively make room for everyone.

outro.script: That's Day 327. Tomorrow, we'll explore feeling what others feel—empathy. Until then, notice who might need more active inclusion.

growTrack.title: Inclusion Practice - Who Needs Welcome?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and act on inclusion opportunities
growTrack.activity: In your environments—work, social, community—who is present but not included? What barriers prevent their participation? What's one action you could take to create more belonging for someone?
